# Papercuts — legeos

Small frictions hit while working, logged in the moment (D-027). None of these blocked anything; together they show where the project needs sanding down. Newest first.

- 2026-08-21 [claude] Partitioning file ownership across five parallel agents left the shared vocabulary crates (lege-types, lege-client/src/proxies) owned by nobody, so a cross-cutting contract could not be added by anyone: the checkpoint protocol was documented and implemented on both ends but had no wire transport, and the session daemon correctly reported it was barred from adding one. Whoever partitions parallel work should own the shared vocabulary themselves and settle cross-cutting contracts up front, as was done for org.legeos.Resources1 — that one worked precisely because it was fixed before the agents started.  `@legeos.papercut.partitioning-file-ownership-across-five/1`
- 2026-08-21 [claude] ADR-0012 landed as a markdown ADR without a matching ledger record, so for several commits the ledger kept asserting cosmic-comp was a pinned fork (D6) and cosmic-greeter the greeter (D10), both active, while the tree said otherwise. Nothing flagged it — a decision recorded only in docs/adr/ is invisible to validation. Worth a check that every docs/adr/NNNN-*.md has a corresponding decision record.  `@legeos.papercut.adr-0012-landed-as-a-markdown-adr-without-a/1`

## Not about this project

Frictions with something else — a tool, a harness — hit while working here. They are logged where they were hit; `akr papercut collate --about <subject>` is how the project that owns the subject gathers them.

- 2026-08-17 [claude] (akr) Promoting decisions to active with `akr revise <key> --state active` in text mode printed only "nothing written" — the actual reason (V-021: active decision cites nothing; and V-005: supported_by may not target a constraint, use implements) only appeared with --format json. Text mode should print the blocking diagnostics too.  `@legeos.papercut.promoting-decisions-to-active-with-akr-revise/1`
